title: Why is No CORS the default state for CORS settings attributes?
body: Recently, I noticed some rather counter-intuitive behavior when attempting to manipulate image data on an HTML canvas. Under normal circumstances, when you set the `src` of an `img` element to an image from a cross-origin site and draw the resulting image to a canvas with [`CanvasRenderingContext2D#drawImage`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/drawImage), the canvas becomes tainted (no longer "origin-clean") and scripts can no longer read pixel data from it with methods such as [CanvasRenderingContext2D#getImageData](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/getImageData). This is normal and expected behavior, as doing otherwise would violate the same-origin policy by allowing scripts on one origin to read image data from another origin. In order to explicitly allow cross-origin access to image data, sites may send CORS headers such as [Access-Control-Allow-Origin](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Access-Control-Allow-Origin) in their responses to requests for those images. Now here's the counter-intuitive part: even if a site _does_ send a `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` header with an image, access to that image data is _still_ not allowed by default if that image was loaded via an `` element. Working example: https://jsfiddle.net/eaxxqLao/9/ Screenshot: ![Cross-origin image being sent with `access-control-allow-origin: *` but access is still not allowed.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1876931/37842801-244f917e-2e91-11e8-9434-1c0137588ebe.png) Only if you explicitly set the `` element's `crossorigin` attribute is access to the image data allowed. After reading through the spec, I determined the reason for this. The `crossorigin` attribute on the `img` element [is a CORS settings attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#attr-img-crossorigin). The [missing value default for CORS settings attributes is "No CORS"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#cors-settings-attributes:missing-value-default). This causes the resulting request's mode [to be set to "no-cors"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#create-a-potential-cors-request), which causes the resulting response [to be an opaque filtered response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-concept-filtered-response-opaque%E2%91%A1) (even though the appropriate CORS response headers are sent), leading to this unintuitive behavior. So my question is: why is the missing value default for CORS settings attributes set to "No CORS" in the first place? Why not "anonymous"? Would there be any downsides to making "anonymous" the missing value default? **TL;DR:** When an `` element's source image is served with the header `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, why does the spec still require me to explicitly set the `crossorigin` attribute on the `` element before I can access the image data via a ``?
